name: John Wesley Dobbs & Family
role: Voting rights advocate, 'Mayor of Auburn Avenue'
summary: Coined the term 'Sweet Auburn' and led major voter registration drives in Atlanta's Black community. Grandfather of Maynard Jackson, Atlanta's first Black mayor.
facts: Often called 'The Mayor of Auburn Avenue,' coined the term 'Sweet Auburn'
Grand Master of Georgia's Prince Hall Masons
Founded the Atlanta Civic and Political League and the Georgia Voters League in the 1930s-40s
Led a voter-registration drive recognized as the birth of Atlanta's modern Civil Rights Era
Helped desegregate the Atlanta Police Department in 1948
Grandfather of Maynard Jackson, Atlanta's first Black mayor

name: Clara Maxwell Cater Pitts
summary: Superintendent of the Carrie Steele Orphans Home. Modernized its operations and secured United Way funding. The orphanage was renamed in her honor in 1950.
facts: Served as superintendent of the Carrie Steele Orphans Home
Modernized operations and relocated the facility to Roy Street in southwest Atlanta
Secured funding through the Atlanta Community Chest (later the United Way)
In 1950 the orphanage was renamed the Carrie Steele Pitts Home in her honor
An Atlanta Public School was also named in her honor

name: Moses Amos
role: First licensed Black pharmacist in Georgia
summary: In 1911 became the first African American granted a Georgia druggist license. Built Gate City Drug Store on Auburn Avenue into a hub of mentorship.
facts: In June 1911 passed the Georgia State pharmacy exam, first African American granted a druggist license
Proprietor of the Gate City Drug Store on Auburn Avenue
In 1914 hired the first African American woman to work in a public place in Atlanta
Employed nine young men who went on to earn degrees in pharmacy, medicine, and dentistry

name: Dinah Watts Pace
summary: Born enslaved in Athens, GA. Founded one of Georgia's earliest orphanages for African American children. Graduated from Atlanta University in 1884.
facts: Born enslaved in Athens, Georgia in 1853
As a teenager started a Sunday School that grew into Reed Street Baptist Church (today Paradise Missionary Baptist Church)
Graduated from Atlanta University in 1884
Founded the Covington Colored Orphans Home in 1890
Died in 1933 at age 80; Dinah Pace Road is named in her honor

name: First Lt. Walter Westmoreland
summary: Morehouse College graduate who flew with the 332nd Fighter Squadron during WWII. Shot down on October 13, 1944, returning from an escort mission over Germany.
facts: Graduated from Morehouse College and earned a master's from Atlanta University
Flew with the 332nd Fighter Squadron of the 302nd Group during World War II
The 332nd painted their aircraft tails solid red, the legendary 'Red Tail Flyers'
Shot down October 13, 1944, returning from an escort mission to Blechhammer, Germany

name: Adrienne Herndon
role: Educator and actor, wife of Alonzo Herndon
summary: Among the first African American faculty at Atlanta University. Made her professional acting debut in Boston in 1904. Designed the Herndon family's Diamond Hill mansion.
facts: One of the first African American faculty members at Atlanta University, teaching elocution
Made professional acting debut in Boston in 1904 under the stage name Anne Du Bignon
Graduated from the School of Dramatic Arts in New York City in 1908
Designed Diamond Hill, the Herndon family's fifteen-room mansion in Atlanta
Wife of Alonzo Franklin Herndon

name: Alonzo Franklin Herndon
role: Entrepreneur, founder of Atlanta Life Insurance
summary: Born enslaved in Social Circle, Georgia. Founded Atlanta Life Insurance Company in 1905, the largest Black-owned insurance company in the U.S.
facts: Born enslaved in Social Circle, Georgia
Founded Atlanta Life Insurance Company in 1905, the largest Black-owned insurance company in the U.S.
Transformed a $1.25 shoeshine cloth into a barbershop empire serving Atlanta's elite
His Classical Revival mansion on University Drive is now a National Historic Landmark
At his death, his estate was valued at over $500,000

name: George 'Union' Wilder
role: Victim of the 1906 Atlanta Race Massacre
summary: Union Army veteran killed defending his home during the 1906 Atlanta Race Massacre. His stand in Brownsville helped slow the rioters.
facts: Union Army veteran who settled in Brownsville, Atlanta after the Civil War
Killed September 22, 1906, defending his home with a muzzle-loaded musket against a white mob
His stand in Brownsville is credited with slowing the rioters and stemming their momentum
The massacre killed at least 12 African Americans, the true toll was likely higher

name: Rev. A. D. & Jennie Williams
role: Grandparents of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.
summary: A.D. Williams was the second pastor of Ebenezer Baptist Church, growing it from a handful to 750+ members. Co-founded the Atlanta NAACP in 1917.
facts: Second pastor of Ebenezer Baptist Church, grew congregation from a handful to over 750
Developed Ebenezer as both religious institution and center for political activity
Helped establish the Atlanta branch of the NAACP in 1917 and served as president
Jennie Celeste Parks Williams led Ebenezer's missionary society
Maternal grandparents of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.

name: Rev. & Mrs. Martin Luther King Sr.
role: Parents of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.
summary: Pastor of Ebenezer Baptist Church for 44 years. Led a voting-rights march on Atlanta City Hall in 1936.
facts: Pastor of Ebenezer Baptist Church for 44 years
Led a voting-rights march on Atlanta City Hall in 1936 and won equalization of teacher pay
Served on the boards of Atlanta University and Morehouse College
Alberta Williams King started the Ebenezer choir; killed by a gunman during Sunday worship in 1974
Parents of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.

name: Henry 'Hank' Aaron
role: Baseball legend and civil rights supporter
summary: Broke Babe Ruth's career home run record despite death threats. Used his fame to champion civil rights. Awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom.
facts: Surpassed Babe Ruth's career home run record despite racial insults and death threats
First Black American in a senior management role in baseball (Atlanta Braves front office)
Served as a director on the board of the NAACP
Awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by President George W. Bush
Inducted into the International Civil Rights Walk of Fame at the MLK Jr. National Historic Park

name: Julian Bond
summary: SNCC co-founder, Georgia legislator, first president of the Southern Poverty Law Center, and chairman of the NAACP.
facts: Among the first leaders of SNCC, organizing sit-ins and boycotts
Elected to Georgia House in 1965 but barred for opposing Vietnam War; won his seat via Supreme Court ruling
Served in both the Georgia House and Senate
First president of the Southern Poverty Law Center
Chairman of the national NAACP

name: Congressman John Lewis
role: Civil rights leader and U.S. Congressman
summary: Served in U.S. House from 1987 until his death. Chairman of SNCC, one of the 'Big Six' organizers of the 1963 March on Washington.
facts: Served in the U.S. House for Georgia's 5th district from 1987 until his death in 2020
Participated in the 1960 Nashville sit-ins and the Freedom Rides
Chairman of SNCC from 1963 to 1966
One of the 'Big Six' organizers of the 1963 March on Washington
Widely regarded as the conscience of the U.S. Congress
